1000_times_faster_operations_bring_relia.summary: A new single‑cycle method developed at Chalmers University of Technology accelerates bosonic quantum operations by over a thousand times, moving fault‑tolerant quantum computing nearer.
highlights: Quantum lattice gates enable complex operations in a single driving cycle
The technique works on existing superconducting quantum circuit platforms
Potential to reduce error rates and speed up fault‑tolerant quantum computers

lunar_foundation_model_launch.headline: NASA‑IBM Lunar Foundation Model promises unprecedented moon surface maps
lunar_foundation_model_launch.summary: A new open‑source AI system unifies multimodal lunar data, delivering finer crater, ice, and volcanic feature maps for upcoming missions.
highlights: Lunar Foundation Model (LFM) integrates optical, laser, radar, and spectrometer data across 2 million map tiles
LFM outperforms SwinV2‑B by up to 19% in crater detection using half the training labels
Ice prospectivity errors drop up to 22% compared with previous models
Model and benchmark dataset SomBench are released on Hugging Face for community use

continuous_black_hole_radio_video.headline: AI‑Powered Video Reveals Blazar 3C 345 Jets Defy Shock‑Wave Theory
continuous_black_hole_radio_video.summary: A new AI algorithm called kine turns 27 years of VLBI data on blazar 3C 345 into a continuous video, showing bright knots move with the plasma rather than as faster shock waves.
highlights: kine reconstructs a 27‑year video from 116 VLBA observations with four‑times higher resolution
bright knots in 3C 345 travel at speeds comparable to the surrounding relativistic jet
polarization data indicate knots are magnetically energized, not shock‑compressed regions

rewetting_peatlands_may_curb_warming_dri.headline: Rewetting Peatlands Could Slash Temperature‑Driven CO₂ Emissions
rewetting_peatlands_may_curb_warming_dri.summary: A global analysis of 276 site‑years shows that raising water tables to within 20 cm of the surface markedly reduces peatland CO₂ releases under warming.
highlights: CO₂ emissions rise sharply when water tables fall below 60–75 cm and temperatures increase
Water tables at 20 cm or higher dampen the temperature‑driven CO₂ surge
Daily data from 113 site‑years confirm that higher water levels curb short‑term temperature sensitivity

mercury_shrinking_faster.headline: Mercury May Have Shrunk Up to 23 km Since Forming, New Study Finds
mercury_shrinking_faster.summary: A new analysis suggests Mercury’s radius decreased by as much as 23 km—10‑30 percent more than earlier estimates—due to hidden impact‑debris effects.
highlights: Mercury’s shrinkage could be up to 23 km, roughly 30 percent greater than prior models
Researchers used MESSENGER data to map surface roughness and reveal obscuring debris
The finding implies a larger metallic core, possibly altering estimates of core composition
BepiColombo will soon test these results with higher‑resolution observations

2609_11306v1.headline: New General Formula Links Primordial Black Hole Clustering to Non‑Gaussianity
2609_11306v1.summary: Researchers present an analytical expression for the PBH two‑point correlation function that works for any local‑type non‑Gaussianity, connecting clustering to the primordial trispectrum.
highlights: Derives a universal PBH bias parameter valid for arbitrary local non‑Gaussianity
Applies the framework to ultra‑slow‑roll inflation, curvaton and modulated reheating scenarios
Extends to broad power spectra, enabling cross‑mass‑scale correlation analysis

desi_baryoncdm_2026_09_11.headline: DESI Tightens Limits on Baryon‑CDM Perturbations, Dark Energy Preference Holds
desi_baryoncdm_2026_09_11.summary: Using DESI full‑shape data, researchers place tight constraints on baryon‑cold‑dark‑matter density and velocity biases, confirming that dark‑energy evolution signals remain unchanged.
highlights: b_{\delta_{bc}}=5\pm6 and b_{v^2_{bc}}=-0.031\pm0.023 for the LRG2 sample in a DESI‑only analysis
Switching to a w_0w_aCDM model yields b_{\delta_{bc}}=2\pm5 and b_{v^2_{bc}}=-0.032\pm0.022
Adding velocity‑divergence bias gives b_{\theta_{bc}}≈-760 with large uncertainty
Constraints on w_0 and w_a are virtually identical after marginalizing over baryon‑CDM modes

2609_10661v1.headline: Dark Matter‑Baryon Separability Framework Predicts Dynamics of Almost‑Dark Galaxy TTT J1237327+143535
2609_10661v1.summary: A new separability model links dark matter deficiency and baryon depletion, offering testable predictions for the dynamics of the ultra‑faint galaxy TTT J1237327+143535.
highlights: Extends the Dark Matter‑Baryon Separability Condition to a branch describing preferential baryonic loss
Derives dynamical consistency relations involving σₗₒₛ, M_dyn, baryonic fraction, and mass‑to‑light ratio
Connects halo mass estimates to the expected globular‑cluster population in the Virgo Cluster

2609_11056v1.headline: New EFT Method Reconstructs Ultralight Axion Oscillations with Sub‑percent Accuracy
2609_11056v1.summary: Researchers have implemented an effective field theory approach that captures relativistic axion oscillations, achieving sub‑percent agreement with exact solutions.
highlights: First EFT‑based technique to resolve rapid axion oscillations
Wavefunction representation includes relativistic corrections
Computational speed rivals existing methods while improving precision

arxiv_2609_10696v1.headline: Primordial Black Holes May Experience Runaway Growth During Cosmic Reheating
arxiv_2609_10696v1.summary: New analytical models show that PBH absorption of plasma during reheating can trigger runaway mass increase, altering early‑universe black‑hole evolution.
highlights: Reheating dynamics modify the critical condition for PBH runaway absorption
Two regimes identified: growth during reheating or delayed growth after radiation domination
A composition law links mass‑growth mechanisms across successive cosmological eras

xrism_perseus_icm.headline: XRISM Maps Chaotic Motions in Perseus Cluster Core via Resonant Scattering
xrism_perseus_icm.summary: XRISM observations reveal that small‑scale random motions dominate the intracluster medium within the central 60 kpc of the Perseus cluster, challenging bulk‑flow interpretations.
highlights: Resonant scattering of the Heα w line shows central flux suppression and outer‑region enhancement
Velocity dispersion matches line‑broadening measurements, indicating turbulence‑dominated motions
Simulations favor isotropic or radial motions over tangential ones

fuzzy_dm_constraints.headline: Euclid data tighten fuzzy dark matter mass limits via dwarf galaxy globular clusters
fuzzy_dm_constraints.summary: Using Euclid Early Release Observations of dwarf galaxies in the Fornax and Perseus clusters, researchers constrain the ultra‑light dark matter particle mass to around 10⁻²² eV.
highlights: Globular clusters in Fornax show no orbital decay for particle masses m₍₂₂₎≤1.46⁺⁰·⁵¹₋₀·₃₂
Perseus clusters yield a similar bound of m₍₂₂₎≤1.09⁺⁰·¹₄₋₀·₂₁
The fuzzy dark matter model modifies halo density profiles and dynamical friction, alleviating the classic globular‑cluster

nonreciprocal_active_matter_2026_09_11.headline: Non‑reciprocal forces keep mixed colloids in perpetual motion
nonreciprocal_active_matter_2026_09_11.summary: Researchers at Tokyo University of Science discovered that size‑asymmetric electrohydrodynamic forces prevent aggregation, enabling continuous reorganization of mixed colloidal particles.
highlights: Mixed particles of 1 µm and 1.5 µm radii form asymmetric, self‑propelled pairs under an alternating electric field
Larger particles attract smaller ones more strongly, creating non‑reciprocal interactions that break apparent Newton’s third law
Clusters continuously fragment and rearrange instead of coarsening into static aggregates

arxiv_2609_10663v1.headline: Nautilus Space Observatory to Map Kuiper‑Belt‑to‑Oort‑Cloud Transition and Boost Cislunar Resilience
arxiv_2609_10663v1.summary: A two‑layer mission using a 4 m Nautilus Quattro Imaging unit and a network of ~50 cm telescopes will characterize near‑Earth small bodies while surveying distant Solar System objects to Vmag ~30.
highlights: 4 m Nautilus Quattro Imaging unit will conduct deep‑search surveys reaching Vmag ~30
~50 cm wide‑field telescopes in cislunar orbit will monitor meter‑ to decameter‑scale objects
Combined program aims to resolve fading planetary‑defense targets and map the Kuiper‑Belt‑to‑Oort‑Cloud transition

bh_galaxy_correlations.headline: GIZMO‑SIMBA and TNG‑Cluster Simulations Reveal Divergent Black‑Hole Growth Paths in Massive Clusters
bh_galaxy_correlations.summary: Zoom‑in simulations from GIZMO‑SIMBA and TNG‑Cluster show contrasting SMBH‑galaxy co‑evolution, with early torque‑limited growth versus delayed feedback‑regulated assembly.
highlights: GIZMO‑SIMBA predicts torque‑limited SMBH accretion that locks the halo‑mass–BH‑mass relation by z=3.0
TNG‑Cluster features early thermal suppression followed by kinetic winds that hard‑quench star formation
Both models reproduce the observed decoupling of BHAR and SFR in massive cluster ellipticals

distant_proto_supercluster.headline: Earliest Proto‑Supercluster COSMOS‑z3.1‑A Unveiled at Cosmic Web Intersection
distant_proto_supercluster.summary: Astronomers have identified COSMOS‑z3.1‑A, a proto‑supercluster seen when the universe was 2.1 billion years old, weighing about 5,000 times the Milky Way.
highlights: Mass of COSMOS‑z3.1‑A is ~5,000 times that of the Milky Way
Located at the junction of multiple filaments in the cosmic web
3D mapping used DECam, DESI, GMOS, and DEIMOS spectrographs

blue_light_breaks_rule.headline: Blue Light Defies Rule‑of‑Five, Unlocking 3D Drug Scaffolds
blue_light_breaks_rule.summary: A Bristol team used blue‑light‑driven photocatalysis to overturn the rule‑of‑five, creating rigid sp³‑rich bicyclic scaffolds for drug design.
highlights: Photocatalyst absorbs ordinary blue light and transfers energy to nitrogen‑containing 1,5‑dienes
Acetyl group on nitrogen directs regiodivergent cyclization, breaking the long‑standing rule‑of‑five
The method produced a 3D analogue of an experimental cognitive‑enhancement drug
Further functionalization shows the scaffolds can be diversified for medicinal chemistry

2609_10665v1.headline: Aletheia Emulator Delivers Percent-Level Halo Mass Function Predictions Across Dark Energy Models
2609_10665v1.summary: A new Gaussian‑process emulator predicts halo abundances with percent‑level accuracy for ΛCDM and a wide range of dynamical dark‑energy cosmologies.
highlights: Emulator uses evolution mapping to separate shape and evolution parameters
Trained on 100 flat ΛCDM simulations but applicable to curvature and quintessence models
Achieves per cent‑level accuracy over diverse masses and redshifts

pluto_atmosphere_collapse.headline: Pluto’s Nitrogen Atmosphere Shows 16% Pressure Drop, Hinting at Seasonal Collapse
pluto_atmosphere_collapse.summary: A uniform analysis of stellar occultations from 1988 to 2023 reveals Pluto’s lower atmosphere pressure fell 16% between 2022 and 2023, suggesting the onset of atmospheric collapse.
highlights: Pluto’s lower atmosphere pressure dropped 16% in 2022‑2023 after remaining stable since the 2015 New Horizons flyby
The decline was identified by re‑analyzing 10 new occultations alongside historic data from over 15 telescopes
Upper atmospheric haze cleared while lower‑atmosphere haze began to dissipate, indicating cooling and nitrogen snow formation

wasps_disappearing_summer.headline: British wasps vanish amid record heatwaves, scientists warn
wasps_disappearing_summer.summary: British wasps have become scarce this summer as unprecedented heatwaves and erratic temperatures threaten their survival and reduce adult size.
highlights: Extreme ground temperatures exceeded 50 °C, surpassing the wasps’ critical thermal maximum of ~45 °C.
The Big Wasp Survey has not yet collected data for 2026, leaving the decline anecdotal.
Remaining wasps observed are unusually small, indicating heat‑accelerated development and limited larval nutrition.
Researchers urge public participation in the Wasp Picnic Survey 2026 to gather observations.

2609_10622v1.headline: Variable Diffusion Ratio Resolves 2017 Cosmic Ray Depression Puzzle
2609_10622v1.summary: Researchers used AMS-02 data and a Parker transport model to explain the 2017 galactic cosmic ray proton dip by adjusting diffusion parameters.
highlights: The 2017 GCR proton flux drop coincided with strong CMEs as Solar Cycle 24 neared minimum
A steady‑state Parker framework matched AMS‑02 observations but gave unrealistic rigidity dependence
Allowing the perpendicular‑to‑parallel diffusion ratio to drop during CME activity restored expected turbulence behavior

pfas_to_silver_fluoride.headline: Electrical Pulses Turn PFAS Waste Into Recyclable Silver Fluoride
pfas_to_silver_fluoride.summary: Rice University researchers use flash‑encapsulated fluorination to capture fluoride from firefighting foam waste, producing silver fluoride for industrial use.
highlights: Flash‑encapsulated fluorination uses short electrical pulses to release fluorine from PFAS adsorbed on activated carbon
A porous quartz‑fiber barrier separates carbon and silver, preventing reduction of silver fluoride
The process removes >99.9% of fluoride, with 90% recovered as usable silver fluoride

mercury_magnetic_crust_2026.headline: Mercury’s Crustal Magnetism Mostly Explained by Present-Day Induced Fields
mercury_magnetic_crust_2026.summary: A new model using MESSENGER data shows that over 85% of Mercury’s northern crustal magnetic field can be accounted for by induced magnetization from its weak core field.
highlights: Induced magnetization can explain >85% of the crustal field north of 38° N
Magnetization strength correlates with crustal thickness up to ~30 km, not just iron content
Areas requiring remanent magnetization may reflect ancient asteroid‑delivered iron

ttr_aggregation_mechanism_2026.headline: Scientists Uncover Alternative Unfolding Pathway of Disease‑Linked Transthyretin Protein
ttr_aggregation_mechanism_2026.summary: Researchers at Scripps Research identified a second route by which the tetrameric TTR protein disassembles, potentially accelerating amyloid aggregation in rare hereditary forms.
highlights: Alternative pathway bypasses dimer intermediates, directly yielding monomers
Over 100 TTR variants were tested across urea and pH gradients
Cryogenic‑electron microscopy confirmed the expanded transition state
Pathway is favored in acidic lysosomal conditions and some brain‑associated mutations

wood_formation_climate.headline: Faster Wood Formation Trumps Longer Growing Seasons in Warming Forests
wood_formation_climate.summary: A global analysis of over 50,000 conifer samples shows that the speed of xylem cell production influences annual wood growth more than extended growing periods.
highlights: Rate of xylem cell production had a stronger impact on annual wood volume than season length
Warmer temperatures above ~6 °C slowed cell production, likely due to reduced water availability
Boreal forests benefit from faster growth, while Mediterranean and temperate forests see limited gains

martian_gullies_non_water_mechanism.headline: CO₂ Frost Fluidization Drives Active Gullies on Mars, Not Water
martian_gullies_non_water_mechanism.summary: New pre‑print analysis shows seasonal CO₂ frost, not liquid water, carves the rapidly changing gullies near Mars’ south‑pole Sisyphi Cavi.
highlights: Spectral data from CRISM and OMEGA show no 1.5 µm water absorption during spring melt
Geyser activity peaks before gully formation, ruling out the Kieffer geyser mechanism
CO₂ sublimation creates a lubricating gas layer that lets ice‑dirt slabs slide down slopes

foraminifera_spiral_flipping_evolutionar.institution: Researchers featured in Quanta Magazine article
foraminifera_spiral_flipping_evolutionar.headline: Global Foraminifera Shell Chirality Flips Reveal Hidden Evolutionary Sweeps
foraminifera_spiral_flipping_evolutionar.summary: A new synthesis of 56 million years of fossil data shows that sudden, worldwide switches in shell coiling direction likely mark rapid population sweeps of cryptic foram species.
highlights: Foraminifera shells switched coiling direction simultaneously across Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans
Pulleniatina obliquiloculata displayed rapid flips every few thousand years over the past 860,000 years
Genetic studies suggest cryptic species with slight fitness advantages can dominate globally, akin to viral variants

dense_galaxies_bubble_early_universe.headline: Dense Galaxy Overdensity May Have Carved First Reionization Bubble at z≈10.5
dense_galaxies_bubble_early_universe.summary: A group of 18 galaxies at redshift 10.5 observed by JWST’s JADES survey appears to create a ~6 cMpc ionized bubble, hinting at early cosmic reionization.
highlights: The overdensity contains 18 galaxies, four times the typical field density at redshift 10.5.
Lyman‑alpha transmission rises toward the core, indicating an ionizing bubble roughly 6 cMpc in radius.
Stellar masses and star‑formation rates are modestly higher than field galaxies but not extreme.

ai_hidden_proteins_nature_2026.headline: AI uncovers hidden GPCR-like protein TM184C that mediates intercellular bridges and autophagy
ai_hidden_proteins_nature_2026.summary: Researchers used AI to compare 214 million predicted protein structures, revealing the hidden GPCR-like protein TM184C that regulates cell‑cell bridges and stress‑response autophagy.
highlights: AI compared over 214 million predicted protein shapes to find hidden GPCR family members
TM184C localizes to intracellular vesicles and drives formation of microtubule‑linked cell bridges
Disrupting TM184C reduces intercellular connections and alters autophagy markers
Human TM184C rescued yeast lacking Hfl1, showing a conserved billion‑year function

new_ice_form_neptune_uranus.headline: New Hexagonal Superionic Ice Phase Unveiled, Illuminating Neptune and Uranus Interiors
new_ice_form_neptune_uranus.summary: Researchers recreated extreme planetary conditions in a diamond‑anvil cell, discovering a hexagonal close‑packed superionic ice that may reshape models of ice‑giant interiors.
highlights: Ice adopts a hexagonal close‑packed (hcp) oxygen lattice above 200 GPa and 1,800 K
The hcp phase replaces the previously known face‑centered cubic (fcc) superionic ice
Experiments used laser heating and X‑ray diffraction at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility

sma_muscle_loss_drug_approval.headline: FDA Approves Isembyld, First Therapy Targeting Muscle Loss in SMA
sma_muscle_loss_drug_approval.summary: Scholar Rock’s Isembyld received FDA approval for adults and children with SMA, showing significant motor skill gains when added to SMN2‑targeting treatments.
highlights: Isembyld approved by the FDA for patients aged 2 years and older
First drug to inhibit myostatin and address muscle loss in spinal muscular atrophy
Late‑stage trial showed motor‑skill improvement versus decline in placebo

grass_genome_assembly_2026.institution: Donald Danforth Plant Science Center et al.
grass_genome_assembly_2026.headline: Chromosome‑Level Genome of Streptochaeta Rewrites Grass Evolution History
grass_genome_assembly_2026.summary: A chromosome‑level genome of the tropical grass Streptochaeta spicata reveals an ancient allopolyploid event that reshapes the early evolutionary timeline of all grasses.
highlights: Researchers assembled a chromosome‑level genome for Streptochaeta spicata, a basal grass lineage.
Comparative analysis shows the ancestral grass genome underwent an allopolyploid duplication.
The duplication signature persists in modern cereals such as rice, wheat, and maize.
Findings published in Nature Communications (2026) provide a new framework for crop‑genomics research.

interfacial_water_photocatalysis_tio2.headline: Weaker water‑TiO₂ bonds boost photocatalytic hydrogen production
interfacial_water_photocatalysis_tio2.summary: A study using infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry shows that weaker water‑TiO₂ interactions and flexible hydrogen‑bond networks enhance interfacial water reactivity for H₂ evolution.
highlights: Weaker water‑TiO₂ interactions correlate with higher H₂ evolution rates
More flexible hydrogen‑bond networks increase water reactivity
Infrared spectroscopy combined with real‑time mass spectrometry quantified interfacial water structure
Normalization by surface area and water layers isolated true catalytic activity

breast_cancer_pill_trial_failure.headline: AstraZeneca’s Breast Cancer Pill Fails Pivotal First‑Line Trial
breast_cancer_pill_trial_failure.summary: The camizestrant‑Etcamah combination did not extend progression‑free survival versus standard therapy in the SERENA‑4 trial of ER‑positive, HER2‑negative advanced breast cancer.
highlights: Camizestrant plus a partner drug was tested as first‑line treatment for advanced disease
The SERENA‑4 trial showed no improvement in progression‑free survival compared with standard care
The drug had received accelerated approval in the U.S. for mutation‑driven resistance

copper_uti_mechanism.institution: Texas A&M College of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences
copper_uti_mechanism.headline: Texas A&M Researchers Harness Copper to Combat Antibiotic‑Resistant UTIs
copper_uti_mechanism.summary: Scientists at Texas A&M are studying how the immune system’s copper surge attacks urinary tract infections and how bacteria adapt, aiming for new copper‑based therapies.
highlights: The body increases copper levels in urine during infection, creating a toxic environment for bacteria.
UTI‑causing bacteria possess copper‑detoxifying mechanisms but are vulnerable when copper is combined with immune antimicrobials.
Researchers identified an experimental antimicrobial that works better with copper and are modifying it for future therapies.

whole_body_cell_communication_imaging.headline: WHOLISTIC Imaging Reveals Whole‑Body Cellular Communication in Live Zebrafish
whole_body_cell_communication_imaging.summary: Scientists used the WHOLISTIC system to capture second‑by‑second calcium signaling across entire zebrafish bodies, exposing organ‑wide cellular interactions.
highlights: WHOLISTIC records fluorescent calcium activity throughout a living organism in real time
First applied to transparent larval zebrafish and adult Danionella cerebrum
Observed unexpected calcium spikes in chondrocytes during cold exposure and in meninges after ketamine
Captured brainstem‑driven redistribution of blood flow across the whole body

compost_microbe_enzyme_plastic_degradati.headline: Compost Bacterium Yields Enzyme That Breaks Down Polyurethane Foam and Nylon
compost_microbe_enzyme_plastic_degradati.summary: Researchers bioprospected millions of microbes from Kenya landfill, a tropical zoo, larvae guts and compost, uncovering a versatile enzyme that degrades tough plastics.
highlights: 12 enzymes identified, including 10 that degrade polyurethane and 2 that degrade nylon
The most promising enzyme, CC PUR1 from Chelatococcus composti, tolerates up to 80 °C and diverse solvents
Enzyme activity was screened using fluorescence‑activated cell sorting at up to 10,000 cells per second

fertilizers_and_extreme_heat_are_damagin.headline: Mississippi River Fertilizer Runoff and Heat Threaten Gulf Coral Reefs
fertilizers_and_extreme_heat_are_damagin.summary: Isotope analysis of coral cores shows that rising nitrogen from Mississippi fertilizer runoff, combined with extreme heat, has driven recent bleaching and disease in the Gulf’s Flower Garden Banks.
highlights: Over 60% of nitrogen in recent decades traced to the Mississippi River, peaking at 80% in 2023.
Heatwaves in 2016, 2022 and 2023 coincided with massive coral bleaching and disease outbreaks.
Coral skeletons recorded 270 years of nitrogen isotope changes, revealing the shift after 1850 toward anthropogenic sources.

shapeshifting_plant_roots.headline: Shapeshifting Plant Roots Balance Anatomy, Metabolism, and Microbes to Boost Survival
shapeshifting_plant_roots.summary: Researchers at the University of Nottingham discovered that root anatomical complexity and metabolic reprogramming enable plants to remodel roots when colonized by microbes under nutrient stress.
highlights: Root anatomical complexity dictates the ability to remodel in response to microbial colonization
Microbial presence triggers extensive metabolic reprogramming in plant roots
Findings were published in Nature Communications (2026)
Synthetic biology and N6,N6,N6-trimethyl‑L‑lysine could steer beneficial root‑microbe interactions

bat_dna_longevity.headline: Bats’ DNA Reveals Immune Tricks Linked to Exceptional Longevity
bat_dna_longevity.summary: Eight Myotis bat genomes show that heightened immune defenses and rapid cell‑death pathways may underpin decades‑long lifespans, offering clues for human aging research.
highlights: Long‑lived Myotis species possess elevated cancer‑fighting gene activity
Cells from the longest‑lived little brown bat trigger self‑destruction instead of DNA repair when damaged
Genes tied to bat lifespan overlap heavily with those governing viral interactions
Study published in Nature provides the first comparative analysis of eight Myotis genomes

ai_pathology_cancer_detection.headline: Human‑style AI Boosts Cancer Detection Accuracy on Pathology Slides
ai_pathology_cancer_detection.summary: A new AI trained on pathologists' search behavior achieved near‑perfect cancer spotting, outperforming generic models but still yielding notable false‑positive rates.
highlights: Pathology‑o3 identified cancer‑positive slides with 100% sensitivity, versus 87.5% for OpenAI o3.
False‑positive rate was 15.5% for Pathology‑o3, compared with 53.3% for OpenAI o3.
On an independent dataset, sensitivity remained 97.6% and false‑positives dropped to 37.1%.

rhobast_fluorescence.institution: Institute of Organic Chemistry (Ronald Micura group)
rhobast_fluorescence.headline: RhoBAST RNA Flip of G38 Triggers Fluorescence for Super‑Resolution Imaging
rhobast_fluorescence.summary: A single guanosine flip in the tiny RhoBAST RNA activates dye fluorescence, enabling rapid blinking and high‑resolution tracking of RNA in living cells.
highlights: RhoBAST adopts an inverted V‑shape that houses dye between two loops
Guanine residue G38 flips outward upon dye binding, creating space for activation
Fluorescence blinking from the nucleotide flip supports super‑resolution microscopy

feather_dinosaur_poop.headline: Feather Found in Dinosaur Coprolite Sheds Light on Bird Survival After Asteroid
feather_dinosaur_poop.summary: A 66‑million‑year‑old feather preserved in a Montana coprolite may explain why modern birds endured the impact winter that wiped out other dinosaurs.
highlights: The feather was recovered from a 66‑million‑year‑old coprolite discovered in the Hell Creek Formation of northeastern Montana
CT scans at USC revealed feather structure and associated scales and bone fragments from a hesperornithiform bird
Researchers propose that primitive feather insulation, not just aquatic habitat, influenced which bird lineages survived the

embryo_base_editing.institution: Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons
embryo_base_editing.headline: Base Editing Reaches All Cells in Human Embryos but Triggers Unpredictable DNA Damage
embryo_base_editing.summary: A Columbia study shows base editors can modify every cell in early human embryos, yet they also cause unpredictable chromosomal deletions and mosaic mutations.
highlights: Base editing achieved 100% allele transmission to daughter cells in single‑cell embryos
Unintended large‑scale deletions and off‑target edits were observed despite lower frequency than CRISPR
Mosaicism produced embryos with mixed genetic alterations, undermining clinical predictability
High mRNA levels of the editor halted embryo development, revealing dosage‑dependent toxicity

classical_light_quantum_machine.headline: LSU Turns Classical Light into Room‑Temperature Quantum Reservoir for Computing
classical_light_quantum_machine.summary: Physicists at LSU demonstrated that bright classical light, combined with photon‑number‑resolving detection, can act as a robust multiphoton quantum reservoir for information processing at room temperature.
highlights: The optical network accesses multiphoton states containing up to 40 photons
Photon‑number‑resolving detectors extract hidden quantum behavior from noisy classical light
The reservoir learned six distinct mathematical functions without reconfiguring the optical network

first_starburst_size.headline: New Simulations Reveal How Massive Early Universe Starbursts Could Be
first_starburst_size.summary: Researchers modelled primordial gas halos under intense Lyman‑Werner radiation, showing that late‑forming Population III starbursts could reach masses detectable by JWST with gravitational lensing.
highlights: Lyman‑Werner UV photons can suppress molecular hydrogen cooling, delaying collapse until atomic cooling triggers massive star
Simulations predict starburst masses large enough for detection when aided by strong gravitational lensing
JWST has already identified candidate galaxies with signatures of pristine starbursts far later than classic models expected

southern_ocean_carbon_sink_flip.headline: Southern Ocean Could Turn From Carbon Sink to Source Under Mitigation
southern_ocean_carbon_sink_flip.summary: New climate simulations show the Southern Ocean may switch from absorbing CO₂ to releasing it even as global emissions fall.
highlights: Simulations predict a net CO₂ release of about 8.6 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ under a net‑zero scenario and 8.5 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ under sustained
Warming surface waters and declining alkalinity reduce the ocean’s ability to dissolve CO₂, reversing the air‑sea CO₂ gradient
The model shows the flip occurring around year 2154, long after atmospheric CO₂ begins to decline

diamond_melting_point_correction.headline: Laser Shock Experiments Reveal Diamond Melts Over 1,300°F Lower Than Thought
diamond_melting_point_correction.summary: A new ultraviolet‑laser shock study shows diamond’s melting point is more than 1,300 °F lower, aligning measurements with theoretical models.
highlights: Diamond melts at ~12,140 °F (6,727 °C) under 660‑1,060 GPa pressures
The melt occurs without a solid‑carbon intermediate phase
Findings aid nuclear‑fusion capsule design and improve models of Uranus and Neptune interiors

atlantic_hidden_heat_valve.headline: Atlantic "Heat Valve" May Amplify Warming as AMOC Weakens
atlantic_hidden_heat_valve.summary: New research shows the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation acts like a heat valve, and its weakening could trap more heat, boosting global warming.
highlights: Researchers used three climate models that spontaneously generate D‑O‑like oscillations under glacial conditions.
Strong AMOC triggers deep North Atlantic convection, releasing large heat to the atmosphere and space.
Weak AMOC shuts down convection, causing heat buildup in the ocean interior and raising planetary energy.
The “heat‑valve” concept explains why Greenland records show rapid changes while Antarctic records lag.
Future AMOC weakening may amplify warming by throttling this heat‑valve, though modern ice‑free conditions differ from the

nepal_flood_cascading_hazards.headline: Glacier Collapse Triggers Deadly Flood in Nepal, Exposing Cascading Himalayan Hazards
nepal_flood_cascading_hazards.summary: A massive ice‑rock collapse blocked the Bhotekoshi tributary for 18 hours, then burst, killing over 1,000 people and highlighting compound mountain hazards.
highlights: Ice‑rock mass failure created a natural dam on the Lhende Khola tributary
Dam breach unleashed a fast‑moving debris flood that destroyed bridges, roads and hydropower infrastructure
Satellite imagery from Planet Labs and IRDR analysis reconstructed the cascade after the event

ozempic_aging_mouse_study.headline: Semaglutide Extends Lifespan and Reverses Aging Signs in Older Mice
ozempic_aging_mouse_study.summary: Semaglutide treatment in 20‑month‑old female mice prolonged median lifespan by nearly 100 days while improving memory, muscle function and aging biomarkers.
highlights: Semaglutide increased median lifespan by ~100 days in aged mice
Treated mice showed better spatial memory and muscle performance
Inflammation and tissue‑repair gene signatures shifted toward youthful levels
Effects exceeded those of a matched 24% calorie‑restriction diet

cyanobacteria_carbon_sequestration.headline: Tiny cyanobacteria drive majority of ocean carbon sequestration
cyanobacteria_carbon_sequestration.summary: New study shows two‑thirds of deep‑ocean carbon comes from tiny cyanobacteria, overturning the belief that larger phytoplankton dominate the biological carbon pump.
highlights: Sediment traps at 1,000 m in the South China Sea captured carbon linked to surface cyanobacteria
Amino‑acid carbon isotope signatures identified cyanobacterial carbon at depth
Aggregation and ballasting enable cyanobacterial carbon to sink with minimal loss

inflammation_switch_discovery.headline: UCL researchers uncover natural brake that speeds inflammation resolution in humans
inflammation_switch_discovery.summary: A human study shows that blocking soluble epoxide hydrolase boosts epoxy‑oxylipins, reducing intermediate monocytes and accelerating pain relief.
highlights: Blocking sEH with GSK2256294 raised epoxy‑oxylipin levels and cut intermediate monocyte counts
Pain resolved faster despite unchanged redness or swelling
12,13‑EpOME suppressed p38 MAPK, curbing monocyte transformation

sea_level_shorebird_habitat_2026_09_12.headline: Sea‑level rise threatens global shorebird habitats, study warns
sea_level_shorebird_habitat_2026_09_12.summary: A systematic review of 29 shorebird species shows rising seas and coastal squeeze could dramatically shrink critical feeding and nesting wetlands worldwide.
highlights: 78% of examined studies report negative habitat impacts
89% document declines in shorebird populations
Coastal infrastructure blocks wetland migration, intensifying habitat loss

venus_uv_dark_material.headline: Venus’s Pale Yellow Clouds May Hide Extremely Dark UV Absorber
venus_uv_dark_material.summary: Scientists have quantified how strongly the unknown absorber in Venus’s upper clouds must absorb UV‑blue light, sharply narrowing viable organic and inorganic candidates.
highlights: Absorption coefficient reaches ~1,278 cm⁻¹ at 375 nm across 365‑455 nm range
Model suggests a bulk liquid absorber would need ~10 g L⁻¹ if organic, or similarly high concentrations if inorganic
Future missions like the Rocket Lab‑planned Autofluorescence Nephelometer aim to test these constraints in situ

helium_abundance_precision.institution: University of Minnesota Twin Cities (and international collaborators)
helium_abundance_precision.headline: Record‑Precision Measurement of Primordial Helium Sets New Cosmology Standard
helium_abundance_precision.summary: An international team measured the universe’s primordial helium abundance to 0.5% uncertainty using 130 hours on the Large Binocular Telescope.
highlights: Helium abundance determined with 0.5% uncertainty, three times better than previous results
Observations focused on 15 pristine, chemically‑unevolved dwarf galaxies
The MODS spectrographs at the Large Binocular Telescope enabled simultaneous analysis of over 10 helium and 15 hydrogen lines

alzheimer_genome_layer.institution: University of California, San Diego (et al.)
alzheimer_genome_layer.headline: 3D Genome Disruption Revealed as New Layer in Alzheimer’s Disease
alzheimer_genome_layer.summary: Scientists discovered that altered three‑dimensional DNA folding in prefrontal cortex cells of Alzheimer’s patients reshapes gene activity, adding a novel regulatory dimension to the disease.
highlights: Single‑cell GAGE‑seq linked 3D genome contacts with transcription in individual brain cells
AI model Hicformer predicts gene expression changes from chromatin architecture
Alzheimer’s cells show increased compartment mingling and weakened local regulatory interactions

ocean_link_breakdown.headline: Human‑Driven Warming Breaks 400‑Year Indian‑Pacific Ocean Climate Link
ocean_link_breakdown.summary: A new study shows that unprecedented human‑caused warming is unraveling a centuries‑old climate connection between the Indian and Pacific oceans.
highlights: Volcanic eruptions between 1810‑1850 temporarily weakened the Indian‑Pacific coupling, as recorded in coral, tree‑ring and
Climate models indicate the recent decoupling is far more extreme than past volcanic disruptions
The weakening of this ocean link threatens the reliability of tropical rainfall and temperature forecasts

quantum_light_curveball.headline: Hidden Optical Magnus Effect Shifts Laser Interaction in Quantum Light
quantum_light_curveball.summary: Physicists at the Paul Scherrer Institute experimentally demonstrated the optical Magnus effect, showing that a tightly focused laser interacts strongest with a calcium ion slightly off‑center.
highlights: First experimental observation of the optical Magnus effect using a single trapped calcium ion
Interaction point shifts by a few hundred nanometers, dependent only on laser wavelength
Potential to cause errors in qubit control or enable new qubit‑coupling mechanisms

chariklo_ring_change.headline: James Webb Telescope Finds Chariklo’s Rings Becoming More Opaque and Transparent
chariklo_ring_change.summary: Using JWST stellar occultations, researchers observed the inner ring of Chariklo growing more opaque while its outer ring becomes less opaque over the past decade.
highlights: Inner ring opacity increased significantly since 2013
Outer ring opacity decreased in the same period
Observations relied on precise Gaia astrometry and JWST’s L2 orbit

mammoth_site_age.headline: Luminescence dating pushes South Dakota Mammoth Site age beyond 160,000 years
mammoth_site_age.summary: New luminescence dates show the Black Hills sinkhole’s mammoth remains are 160,000‑232,000 years old, far older than previous radiocarbon estimates of ~26,000 years.
highlights: Luminescence dating of surrounding sand yields ages between 160,000 and 232,000 years
Previous radiocarbon dates based on bone apatite ranged 23,000‑42,000 years and were unreliable
Researchers used feldspar OSL after quartz grains were saturated
The study appears in the peer‑reviewed journal Quaternary Research (2026)

primordial_black_hole_gw_constraints.headline: LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA Data Tighten Limits on Inflation‑Driven Primordial Black Holes
primordial_black_hole_gw_constraints.summary: Analysis of O1‑O4a runs places 95% credible upper limits on curvature‑spectrum amplitudes, constraining ultra‑slow‑roll and phase‑transition inflation scenarios.
highlights: No evidence found for ultra‑slow‑roll inflation or inflationary phase‑transition signatures
95% credible upper limits on curvature‑spectrum amplitude across ground‑based detector band
Constraints on primordial black hole abundance now surpass traditional limits

15.headline: CMS delivers most comprehensive Higgs boson test, confirming Standard Model
15.summary: A combined analysis of 138 fb⁻¹ of CMS data finds the Higgs boson’s signal strength 1.01 ± 0.05, fully consistent with Standard Model predictions.
highlights: Signal strength measured as 1.01 ± 0.05, matching the Standard Model expectation
Study combines proton‑proton collisions from 2016‑2018, totaling 138 fb⁻¹
No evidence found for invisible or off‑shell Higgs decays, tightening constraints on new‑physics models

primordial_black_holes_dark_matter_const.headline: INTEGRAL/IBIS 20‑Year Survey Sets New Limits on Asteroid‑Mass Primordial Black Hole Dark Matter
primordial_black_holes_dark_matter_const.summary: A combined spectral‑morphological analysis of 20 years of INTEGRAL/IBIS data finds no hard X‑ray signal from evaporating primordial black holes, tightening dark‑matter constraints.
highlights: First search for inverse‑Compton X‑ray emission from Hawking‑evaporating primordial black holes using INTEGRAL/IBIS
Physically motivated Galactic background model includes cosmic‑ray electrons and unresolved accreting white dwarfs
Constraints cover extended mass functions and rotating primordial black holes across the asteroid‑mass window

3.headline: Ultralight Scalars Could Be Detected via Black Hole Binary Mergers in Galactic Nuclei
3.summary: A new study shows that mergers with mass ratios below 3/10 in the GWTC‑5 catalog can probe ultralight scalars of mass 4×10⁻¹⁴–10⁻¹³ eV.
highlights: Superradiance clouds around spinning black holes provide an extra energy‑dissipation channel during close encounters
Merger rates in dense galactic nuclei become sensitive to ultralight scalar masses
LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA GWTC‑5 data can constrain the scalar mass range [4×10⁻¹⁴, 10⁻¹³] eV

2609_12370v1.headline: Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS Shows Record‑High Water D/H Ratio Linked to Low Metallicity
2609_12370v1.summary: JWST data reveal 3I/ATLAS’s water D/H ratio exceeds comet values, matching models that require sub‑solar metallicity and dense cloud conditions.
highlights: Water D/H ratio in 3I/ATLAS surpasses those measured in Solar System comets
Models reproduce the ratio at metallicities ≤0.5 Z⊙ and densities ≈10⁴ cm⁻³
H₃⁺ deuteration is enhanced in low‑metallicity environments, boosting water deuteration
Methane‑to‑water D/H ratio remains consistent with comet 67P/Churyumov‑Gerasimenko

atomic_c_o_ratio_of_kelt_9b.headline: Atomic C/O Ratio Measured on Ultra‑Hot Jupiter KELT‑9b
atomic_c_o_ratio_of_kelt_9b.summary: Using MAROON‑X spectra, researchers directly measured the atomic carbon‑to‑oxygen ratio of KELT‑9b, finding it significantly lower than solar and stellar values.
highlights: Atomic C/O ratio of KELT‑9b measured as 0.20_{-0.07}^{+0.13}
Stellar C/O ratio is 0.38±0.15, while solar value is 0.59±0.07
Atmosphere shows a thermal inversion and slight metal enrichment
Volatile‑to‑refractory ratio is 1.24× solar, indicating an ice‑to‑rock proxy consistent with the host star

jwst_hubble_27_objects_2026.headline: James Webb and Hubble Reveal 27 Tiny Trans‑Neptunian Objects Preserving Pristine Surfaces
jwst_hubble_27_objects_2026.summary: Joint observations by JWST and Hubble uncovered 27 new TNOs under 40 km, showing unexpectedly unchanged colors despite billions of years of solar‑system evolution.
highlights: 27 new TNOs discovered, all under 40 km in diameter
Smallest object measured at 10 km, still retains original surface color
Both dynamically cold and hot TNOs show identical size distributions
Infrared measurements from JWST isolated size from albedo effects
Findings published as two papers in The Astronomical Journal on Sept. 8

bbn_he_measurement.headline: Large Binocular Telescope Helium Measurement Boosts Cosmology Precision
bbn_he_measurement.summary: A new primordial helium fraction measured by the Large Binocular Telescope validates cosmological parameters independent of big‑bang nucleosynthesis assumptions.
highlights: LBT’s helium fraction measurement matches CMB‑derived constraints without assuming standard BBN
Future CMB surveys need only marginal precision gains to retain BBN‑agnostic power
The result disfavors many proposed solutions to the Hubble and BAO tensions
Neutron‑lifetime anomaly inferred from LBT aligns with bottle‑experiment values, diverging from beam results

lisa_sgwb_eccentric_bbhs.headline: LISA Could Distinguish Eccentric Stellar‑Mass Black Hole Mergers in Stochastic Background
lisa_sgwb_eccentric_bbhs.summary: A new Bayesian model shows that highly eccentric stellar‑mass black‑hole binaries produce a stochastic GW signal detectable by LISA, revealing formation histories and environmental effects.
highlights: If all binaries start with eccentricity e₀ ≳ 0.9 at fₒᵣb = 10⁻⁴ Hz, the SGWB differs clearly from a circular‑binary background.
A thermal eccentricity distribution matches circular predictions only when formation occurs at fₒᵣb = 10⁻⁵ Hz.
Dense gas environments (ρ ≳ 10⁻⁷ g cm⁻³) allow LISA to separate dynamical‑friction effects from vacuum evolution.
A LISA SGWB detection would cap the maximum eccentricity of sBBHs observable by ground‑based detectors.

arxiv_2609_12743v1.headline: Interferometry Rules Out Host Star for Saturn-Mass Free-Floating Planet
arxiv_2609_12743v1.summary: High‑resolution VLTI/GRAVITY observations found no luminous companion within 90 au, strengthening evidence that KMT‑2024‑BLG‑0792/OGLE‑2024‑BLG‑0516 is a truly free‑floating Saturn‑mass planet.
highlights: Measured planet mass: 0.73 (+0.25/‑0.15) Saturn masses.
VLTI/GRAVITY observations set 5σ host‑star mass limit of 0.5–0.6 M☉.
No host detected out to projected separation of 90 au.

definium_lsd_trial_2026.headline: Definium’s LSD Therapy Cuts Anxiety Scores in Second Late‑Stage Trial
definium_lsd_trial_2026.summary: In a 12‑week, double‑blind study, a single 100‑microgram dose of DT120 reduced Hamilton Anxiety scores by 9.8 points versus 4.7 for placebo.
highlights: DT120 produced a 9.8‑point drop on the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale
Placebo group showed a 4.7‑point reduction
The net difference was 5.1 points, matching the first late‑stage trial
Patients reported anxiety improvement as early as day two after dosing

2609_12065v1.headline: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Refines Cosmic Expansion Measurements in New Joint Analyses
2609_12065v1.summary: By jointly analyzing DESI DR2 BAO data with Planck CMB observations and marginalizing BBN uncertainties, researchers obtain tighter constraints on the Hubble constant and effective neutrino species.
highlights: BAO+BBN analysis yields h = 0.6833^{+0.0048}_{-0.0053}.
Adding CMB data tightens h to 0.6823^{+0.0027}_{-0.0026}.
Investigator choices can shift cosmological parameter estimates.

cancer_aging_acceleration.headline: Accelerated Biological Aging Linked to Rising Early‑Onset Cancer in Younger Adults
cancer_aging_acceleration.summary: A new study finds that younger generations show faster biological aging, which correlates with an 8% higher risk of early‑onset solid cancers.
highlights: Younger cohorts exhibited systemic aging up to 92% of one standard deviation higher than older cohorts
Accelerated immune system aging was tied to early‑onset lung cancer, while adipose aging linked to colorectal cancer
Participants with the highest systemic aging faced a 15% greater risk of early‑onset solid cancers

quantum_entanglement_lhc_prl.headline: Oxford Physicists Confirm Quantum Entanglement in Z‑Boson Pairs at the LHC
quantum_entanglement_lhc_prl.summary: Physicists at the University of Oxford have demonstrated that quantum entanglement persists among fleeting Z bosons produced in Higgs decays at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider.
highlights: Entanglement observed in Z‑boson pairs from Higgs boson decays
Measurements made with the ATLAS detector at 13 trillion eV collision energy
Study published in Physical Review Letters, confirming one of the highest‑energy entanglement detections

merons_wse2_scienceadvances.headline: Meron Whirlpools Unveiled in Atom‑Thin Twisted WSe₂ Semiconductor
merons_wse2_scienceadvances.summary: Researchers used high‑resolution vector PFM to directly image meron and antimeron polar nanostructures in a 0.1° twisted bilayer of WSe₂, opening pathways for low‑energy devices.
highlights: Merons and antimerons observed in a marginally twisted bilayer of WSe₂
Twist angle of only 0.1° creates a moiré super‑lattice with circulating polarization
Vector PFM distinguishes twist‑induced effects from strain contributions
Combined experiment and DFT‑based molecular dynamics confirm topological nature

rna_delivery_tags_neurons.headline: m6A Tags Direct RNA Transport to Distant Neurite Branches in Developing Neurons
rna_delivery_tags_neurons.summary: A KAIST team shows that the m6A modification, read by YTHDF2, guides specific RNAs to distal axons, essential for proper neuronal development.
highlights: Deleting Mettl14 in mouse neurons reduces m6A and impairs axon projection and neurite growth.
m6A‑SAC‑seq mapped m6A sites on transcripts linked to axon development and synapse organization.
YTHDF2 partners with FMRP and motor protein KIF5C to transport m6A‑tagged RNAs along neuronal processes.

getting_photons_into_shape_for_reliable_.headline: Engineered Waveguide Reverses Photon Shape to Boost Quantum Communication Efficiency
getting_photons_into_shape_for_reliable_.summary: Researchers at TU Wien propose a dispersion‑engineered waveguide that time‑reverses photon pulses, theoretically raising absorption rates from 54% to near‑100% for quantum networks.
highlights: Photon waveform currently matches a sawtooth shape, limiting absorption to about 54%
Time‑reversing the pulse aligns it with the receiving qubit’s optimal absorption profile
Dispersion‑engineered waveguide can achieve theoretically perfect 100% absorption
Simulations show the passive approach is technically feasible

low_energy_solar_neutrinos.headline: XENONnT Detects Solar Neutrinos at Record‑Low 17 keV Energy
low_energy_solar_neutrinos.summary: Scientists using the dark‑matter detector XENONnT have observed solar neutrinos with energies as low as 17 keV, achieving a 5 σ detection.
highlights: Neutrinos with energies down to 17 keV were identified via electron scattering in XENONnT
The observation reaches the 5 σ statistical threshold, confirming a definitive detection
Previous hints from PandaX‑4T at 2.2 σ are now superseded by XENONnT’s robust result

smbh_binary_gw.headline: 3C 66B and Mrk 501 Emerge as Prime Supermassive Black Hole Binary Targets for SKAO
smbh_binary_gw.summary: A new study shows that 3C 66B and Mrk 501 likely dominate the high‑amplitude tail of the gravitational‑wave background, making them top candidates for individual detection with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory.
highlights: 3C 66B and Mrk 501 stand out from the GW background according to NANOGrav 15‑year data
Models with strong environmental hardening predict more resolvable binaries than purely GW‑driven models
SKAO is forecast to resolve tens of individual SMBH binaries, with 3C 66B robustly detectable

2609_13821v1.headline: Flavour‑Specific Neutrino Self‑Interactions Weaken CMB Coupling Limits
2609_13821v1.summary: A new analysis shows that accounting for neutrino mixing reduces cosmological bounds on flavour‑specific neutrino self‑interactions by factors of √2 or √6.
highlights: Most flavour‑specific interaction scenarios can be modeled with a combined fluid approach
CMB limits on the effective neutrino coupling weaken by √2 when two flavours interact
Limits weaken by √6 for a single interacting flavour, except for νₑ where the fluid model is less reliable

weak_lensing_circular_velocity.headline: Pseudo‑Isothermal Profile Best Fits Weak‑Lensing Circular Velocities of Isolated Galaxies
weak_lensing_circular_velocity.summary: Using KiDS weak‑lensing data, researchers show that only the pseudo‑isothermal dark‑matter model matches circular velocity curves across four baryonic mass bins.
highlights: NFW and Burkert profiles fail to fit all mass bins
Pseudo‑isothermal profile fits all four baryonic mass bins
Analysis based on weak‑lensing measurements from the KiDS survey

gw_diffraction.headline: Extended Dark Objects Reveal Frequency‑Dependent Diffraction of Gravitational Waves
gw_diffraction.summary: Researchers show that dark solitons and dark stars imprint size‑dependent diffraction patterns on gravitational‑wave signals, detectable with current and future observatories.
highlights: Finite‑size lenses alter GW waveforms when lens radius exceeds a few × 10⁶ R₍⊙₎ (M_L/100 M₍⊙₎)^{1/2}
Current LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA data constrain dark‑object masses between 10² M₍⊙₎ and 10⁵ M₍⊙₎
Future next‑generation observatories will surpass present sensitivity, probing broader dark‑sector parameter space

2609_13527v1.headline: Iron’s Incompatibility in Post‑Perovskite Stabilizes Basal Magma Oceans on Super‑Earths
2609_13527v1.summary: First‑principles simulations show iron is strongly excluded from post‑perovskite, making residual melt buoyant and allowing stable basal magma oceans up to four Earth masses.
highlights: Iron‑Mg partition coefficient K_D drops sharply with pressure between 150 GPa and 600 GPa
Residual melt becomes iron‑rich, reversing solid‑liquid density contrast
Basal magma oceans remain gravitationally stable on super‑Earths up to 4 M⊕

2609_13610v1.headline: XMM Survey Finds 66 X‑ray Discontinuities Across 116 CHEX‑MATE Clusters
2609_13610v1.summary: A systematic XMM analysis of the CHEX‑MATE sample reveals 66 surface‑brightness edges, including 32 newly identified features, in roughly 41% of the clusters.
highlights: 66 discontinuities detected, 32 of them newly discovered
Discontinuities appear in 48 of the 116 clusters, with shocks and cold fronts distinguished
~48% of clusters with extended radio emission show X‑ray edges, while ~88% of edge‑bearing clusters host diffuse radio emission

brain_shift_50_75.headline: Midlife Brain Shift Replaces Embryonic Microglia with Inflammatory Cells Between Ages 50‑75
brain_shift_50_75.summary: A new Science study shows that from age 50 to 75 the brain’s immune cells and 3‑D genome structure undergo major remodeling, heightening neurodegeneration risk.
highlights: Sharp decline of embryonic‑origin microglia in the hippocampus between ages 50‑75
Replacement by blood‑like inflammatory microglia‑like cells
Loss of cells maintaining the blood‑brain barrier
Widespread erosion of three‑dimensional genome architecture

smbh_winds_100x.headline: XRISM Reveals Supermassive Black Hole Winds 100× More Powerful Than Expected
smbh_winds_100x.summary: Astronomers using XRISM found that the quasar H1821+643 drives winds whose energy is about one hundred times higher than prior estimates, affecting 300,000 light‑years.
highlights: Winds extend roughly 300,000 light‑years beyond the host galaxy
Turbulent energy rivals several billion supernova explosions
Study based on high‑precision iron‑ion emission lines
Results published in Nature Astronomy

phase3_trutakna_igan.headline: Vera's Trutakna Cuts Kidney Death Risk in Phase 3 Trial
phase3_trutakna_igan.summary: Vera Therapeutics reports that Trutakna stabilized kidney function and lowered kidney‑related death risk over two years in a Phase 3 study of IgA nephropathy patients.
highlights: Trutakna received FDA accelerated approval in July for IgA nephropathy
The Phase 3 trial followed patients for two years
The drug reduced risk of kidney‑related death and other complications

equatorial_storms_warming.headline: Tropical Extreme Rainfall Expands and Persists More as Planet Warms
equatorial_storms_warming.summary: A 45‑year study in Singapore shows that extreme tropical storms are covering larger areas and lasting longer, while peak intensities stay roughly constant.
highlights: Extreme convective storms grew in spatial extent under warming
Storm persistence increased despite unchanged peak rainfall rates
Analysis used 122 rain gauges and weather radar at 100‑meter resolution

ngc1068_hidden_outflow.headline: JWST Uncovers Hidden Supermassive Black Hole Outflow in NGC 1068
ngc1068_hidden_outflow.summary: Infrared JWST/MIRI data reveal a dust‑shrouded gas outflow in NGC 1068 that is up to 100 times more massive than previously measured.
highlights: Mid‑infrared JWST/MIRI spectroscopy detected over 20 ionized‑gas lines and 7 warm H₂ transitions.
The hidden outflow component moves ~300 km s⁻¹ faster and carries most of the mass.
Total outflow mass reaches several million solar masses, with speeds up to 2,000 km s⁻¹.
Modeling shows outflow energetics are up to 100× larger than earlier estimates, likely aided by the radio jet.

mitotic_chromosome_assembly.headline: Pre‑existing Chromatin Domains May Build Mitotic Chromosomes, New Review Shows
mitotic_chromosome_assembly.summary: A review in Trends in Genetics proposes that interphase chromatin domains act as building blocks, reorganized by condensins and physical forces into mitotic chromosomes.
highlights: Historical scaffold model identified non‑histone proteins like condensins and topoisomerase IIα as structural cores.
Recent studies show chromatin physics—electrostatic interactions, Mg²⁺, macromolecular crowding—also shape chromosome
The review suggests interphase chromatin domains serve as pre‑existing building blocks that are cross‑linked during mitosis.

black_hole_hair_ringdown.headline: Hairy Black Holes Could Reveal Their Secrets in Merger Ringdowns
black_hole_hair_ringdown.summary: New theoretical work shows that deviations from the no‑hair theorem would imprint distinct frequencies and decay rates in the gravitational‑wave ringdowns of black‑hole mergers.
highlights: Hayward and Bardeen black‑hole models produce unique ringdown signatures
Ringdown frequency and decay rate differ from standard Kerr black holes
Current detectors lack sensitivity, but future observatories may capture these effects

alma_massive_binary_star_formation.headline: ALMA Captures Formation of Eccentric Massive Protobinary via Core‑Merger Encounter
alma_massive_binary_star_formation.summary: For the first time astronomers tracked two massive young stars orbiting each other while still forming, revealing a highly eccentric, near‑parabolic core‑merger origin.
highlights: The binary IR 07299‑1651 lies ~5,500 light‑years away and shows a 200 au separation with strongly tilted disks.
Combined ALMA, VLA, JWST and VLT data allowed 3‑D orbital reconstruction over an 8‑year baseline.
The eccentric, near‑parabolic orbit and lack of a circumbinary disk rule out simple disk‑fragmentation formation.

novel_particle_beam_muon_gravity_test.headline: Cold muonium beam from PSI may test Einstein’s equivalence principle on second‑generation particles
novel_particle_beam_muon_gravity_test.summary: Physicists at ETH Zurich and the Paul Scherrer Institute have created a high‑intensity, super‑cold muonium beam to measure how muons fall under Earth’s gravity.
highlights: Superfluid helium at –273 °C produces a collimated muonium beam
The beam enables a gravity‑interferometer experiment on second‑generation matter
If muonium’s fall differs, it could hint at a fifth fundamental force

heat_stable_nitrogenase.headline: Heat‑Stable Nitrogenase from Deep‑Sea Archaeon Fixes Nitrogen at 90 °C
heat_stable_nitrogenase.summary: Scientists isolated a nitrogenase from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Methanocaldococcus infernus that remains active up to 98 °C, converting N₂ into ammonia.
highlights: The enzyme stays folded until 90 °C and still functions near 98 °C.
Structural analysis revealed a hybrid metallocofactor combining molybdenum, vanadium and iron features.
Researchers captured a previously unseen “turnover” state in a molybdenum‑containing nitrogenase.
Findings suggest a common ancestral mechanism for nitrogen fixation across all nitrogenase families.

mrna_clumping_prevention.headline: Cells Evolve Codon Strategies to Keep mRNA From Clumping
mrna_clumping_prevention.summary: Researchers show that natural mRNA sequences in bacteria and humans are tuned to reduce sticky interactions, preventing harmful aggregation inside cells.
highlights: Purified E. coli mRNA aggregates in vitro, but native transcripts remain soluble in vivo
Computational redesign of codons increases aggregation propensity, confirming evolutionary pressure
Human abundant mRNAs display the same reduced‑stickiness signature as bacterial transcripts

2609_17315v1.headline: LHAASO Proton Knee Suggests Super‑Heavy Dark Matter but Photon Data Disprove It
2609_17315v1.summary: A relic particle of 5 × 10⁷ GeV could explain LHAASO’s proton hardening at 0.34 PeV and the 3.3 PeV knee, yet its accompanying photons clash with observations.
highlights: Proton spectrum from LHAASO shows a hardening at 0.34 PeV and a knee at 3.3 PeV
A superheavy dark‑matter particle of mass 5 × 10⁷ GeV decaying in the Galactic halo reproduces the proton features
All three hadronic‑interaction‑model reconstructions fit the nucleon‑channel hypothesis
Predicted gamma‑ray cascade exceeds LHAASO diffuse Galactic emission by an order of magnitude
Photon fraction from the model overshoots measured cosmic‑ray photons by two orders of magnitude

2609_16740v1.headline: Nearby Galaxies Show Dark Matter Cores Smaller Than ΛCDM Predictions
2609_16740v1.summary: A study of 136 galaxies from 10^9 to 10^{11.5} M⊙ reveals central dark matter densities far below those expected from ΛCDM simulations.
highlights: Central dark matter densities decline from ~10 kpc in 10^{10} M⊙ galaxies to >50 kpc in 10^{11.5} M⊙ systems
Hydrodynamical simulations invoking baryonic feedback often predict overly steep inner density profiles
The analysis spans radii of 20–50 kpc, providing a comprehensive benchmark across a wide stellar‑mass range

2609_17275v1.headline: Murchison Widefield Array Detects First Unbiased Low‑Frequency Fast Radio Burst
2609_17275v1.summary: A wide‑field imaging survey with the Murchison Widefield Array has captured the first non‑targeted FRB below 300 MHz, confirming a comparable event rate to higher‑frequency detections.
highlights: First FRB detection below 300 MHz from a non‑targeted survey
Imaging‑based search overcomes dispersive delay and scattering challenges
Event rate matches that observed at frequencies above 400 MHz

2609_16394v1.headline: SN 2018ibb’s Light Curve Reveals Dense Circumstellar Matter Around Pair‑Instability Supernova
2609_16394v1.summary: Analysis of SN 2018ibb’s post‑peak light curve shows that interaction with dense circumstellar matter can explain its unexpected blue excess and luminosity break.
highlights: Bolometric luminosity from 150 d after peak matches models with CSM mass‑loss rate 0.01 (v_CSM/1,000 km s⁻¹) M⊙ yr⁻¹
The luminosity break at ~300 d indicates CSM interaction ended, implying a CSM radius of 8.5e16 cm
Progenitor mass loss was enhanced for ~28 (v_CSM/1,000 km s⁻¹)⁻¹ yr before explosion

hotjupiter_ngts10_phasecurve.headline: JWST Reveals Cloud Gaps and Deep Heat Transport on Hot‑Jupiter NGTS‑10 Ab
hotjupiter_ngts10_phasecurve.summary: Using JWST NIRSpec PRISM phase‑curve data, researchers mapped NGTS‑10 Ab’s reflected light and thermal emission, finding anti‑correlated clouds and temperature.
highlights: Thermal emission peaks eastward while reflected light peaks westward, showing distinct atmospheric dynamics
Clouds of micron‑sized silicate particles evaporate over the hottest eastern substellar region
Heat transport efficiency increases with depth, with a measured offset slope of 7.1 ± 1.9 ° per pressure dex

2609_16425v1.headline: Reanalysis Shows 43 GeV Gamma‑Ray Line in Galaxy Clusters Unlikely to Signal Dark Matter
2609_16425v1.summary: A fresh study of Fermi‑LAT data finds the reported 43 GeV line across Virgo, Fornax and Ophiuchus clusters has a broad spatial profile inconsistent with dark‑matter annihilation.
highlights: The excess persists in multiple event‑type partitions and independent data subsets
Uniform surface brightness across the virial region fits the signal better than a central NFW profile
Statistical significance peaks at 2.7 σ after accounting for five morphological models

brown_dwarf_weather.headline: JWST Uncovers Jupiter‑Like Weather Patterns on Brown Dwarf SIMP 0136
brown_dwarf_weather.summary: Using JWST data and principal component analysis, researchers found that SIMP 0136’s atmospheric changes are driven by just two dominant processes.
highlights: Two principal components explain most of the brown dwarf’s brightness variations
The components correspond to temperature shifts and vertical cloud structure changes
Three recurring weather states rotate into view, creating hotter, thinner‑cloud regions and cooler, thicker‑cloud zones

neutron_star_eos.headline: Universal Functional Form Accurately Captures Neutron-Star Equation‑of‑State Across Diverse Models
neutron_star_eos.summary: A new piecewise‑continuous parametrization reproduces tabulated dense‑matter equations of state and matches multimessenger neutron‑star observations with high fidelity.
highlights: Validated against tabulated EoSs from CompOSE and LALSimulation repositories
Bayesian inference using synthetic noise and multimessenger mass‑tidal data constrains parameter correlations
Fits span from very soft to very stiff EoSs, preserving macroscopic neutron‑star observables

2609_16547v1.headline: DESI Spectra Reveal No Optical Absorption from Multi‑State Dark Matter
2609_16547v1.summary: A stacking analysis of 145,087 DESI early‑release spectra finds no optical‑depth signal, setting new limits on magnetic dipole transitions of MeV‑scale dark matter.
highlights: Stacked 145,087 DESI spectra paired with foreground GAMA galaxy groups
Placed 2σ upper limits on magnetic dipole transition cross‑section for ΔE≈3–5 eV
Limits target a few MeV dark matter mass inaccessible to BBN, CMB and direct searches

gw_bias_illustristng300.headline: Machine‑Learned Merger Rates Reveal Stronger Gravitational‑Wave Bias in IllustrisTNG300
gw_bias_illustristng300.summary: A new simulation framework using a machine‑learning emulator calibrated with GALAXYRATE shows BBH mergers preferentially reside in massive, metal‑rich halos, increasing GW bias.
highlights: GW sources exhibit higher bias than the overall galaxy population
The machine‑learned model adds scale‑dependent bias beyond stellar‑mass weighting
Metallicity correlates positively with both GW and galaxy bias

cosmic_noon_miri_wfss.headline: MIRI WFSS Survey of Hubble Ultra Deep Field Reveals 3.3 µm PAH Traces Star Formation at Cosmic Noon
cosmic_noon_miri_wfss.summary: Using JWST's MIRI wide‑field slitless spectroscopy, researchers obtained spectra of 47 galaxies up to redshift 3.712, confirming the 3.3 µm PAH feature as a reliable star‑formation indicator during the Cosmic Noon era.
highlights: Spectra of 47 galaxies with confirmed redshifts were captured using MIRI WFSS in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field
The 3.3 µm PAH luminosities correlate tightly with total infrared luminosity and SED‑derived star‑formation rates
Observations cover redshifts 0.67–3.1, fully spanning the peak star‑formation period known as Cosmic Noon

alzheimer_immune_cells.headline: Lymph‑Node Dendritic Cells Trigger Alzheimer’s Damage, Study Finds
alzheimer_immune_cells.summary: Researchers found that suppressing dendritic cells in lymph nodes protects mice from tau‑driven neurodegeneration, suggesting a new peripheral target for Alzheimer’s therapy.
highlights: In mice lacking lymph‑node dendritic cells, brain tau accumulation persisted but neurodegeneration was markedly reduced
Fewer T cells entered the brains of dendritic‑cell‑deficient mice, linking peripheral immune priming to brain inflammation
The study, published in Nature Neuroscience on September 3, used engineered tau‑linked mouse models to test the hypothesis

jwst_gas_outflows_dead_galaxies.headline: Webb Telescope Finds Record‑Breaking Gas Outflows in Distant Dead Galaxies
jwst_gas_outflows_dead_galaxies.summary: Astronomers using JWST/NIRSpec measured the strongest neutral‑gas outflows ever seen from quiescent galaxies 11‑13 billion years ago, yet most of the gas likely falls back.
highlights: Outflows detected in 13 of 23 massive quiescent galaxies at redshift 2.82–4.62
Neutral Na I D absorption reveals outflow rates 10–100 × higher than ionized gas
The most extreme case, galaxy DD‑236, shows a record‑high outflow linked to an active black hole

human_brain_organoid_mice_shrink.headline: Scientists Replace Missing Mouse Brain Tissue with Human Organoids in Groundbreaking Study
human_brain_organoid_mice_shrink.summary: Researchers transplanted human brain organoids into genetically modified mice lacking most of their cortex, achieving 90% integration and functional growth.
highlights: Genetically modified mice develop only 2% of their cerebral cortex and lack much of the hippocampus
Human cortical organoids were injected into the vacant space, integrating successfully in about 90% of cases
Transplanted mice displayed subtle deficits in fine‑motor skills, working memory, and socialization
The study, published in Nature, offers a new platform for modeling neurodevelopmental disorders

mouse_brain_visual_reconstruction.institution: University of California, Berkeley (or relevant lab)
mouse_brain_visual_reconstruction.headline: UCL researchers reconstruct 10‑second movies from mouse visual‑cortex activity
mouse_brain_visual_reconstruction.summary: Scientists at University College London used calcium imaging of neurons to recreate 10‑second video clips solely from mouse brain signals, revealing how visual input is internally represented.
highlights: Reconstructed videos matched unseen movies using a dynamic neural encoding model
Accuracy improved with data from more individual neurons in the visual cortex
Pixel correlation showed only small timing differences between original and reconstructed clips

240myr_fossil_dinosaur_timeline.headline: Tanzanian Fossil Redefines Timeline of Earliest Dinosaurs
240myr_fossil_dinosaur_timeline.summary: A 240‑million‑year‑old Tanzanian dicynodont named Dinodontosaurus isiyavamanda forces scientists to revise the earliest dinosaur timeline by showing the rocks are younger than previously thought.
highlights: Dinodontosaurus isiyavamanda is the first record of the genus outside South America
The specimen, collected in 1963, lay in the Natural History Museum London for over 60 years before identification
Radiometric dating suggests Tanzanian rock layers are up to 10 million years younger than comparable South African deposits
The study was published in the peer‑reviewed Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology on September 15, 2026

chariklo_ring_dynamics.headline: Chariklo’s Rings Show Rapid Opacity Shifts, New JWST Data Reveal
chariklo_ring_dynamics.summary: Observations by the James Webb Space Telescope in 2022 indicate that Chariklo’s inner and outer rings altered their opacity within just a few years.
highlights: Inner ring became significantly more opaque while the outer ring grew clearer
Study led by the Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia used stellar occultations to track changes
Findings published in Science Advances challenge assumptions about ring stability on small bodies

prime_assembly_universal_gene_therapies.headline: Prime Assembly Enables Multi‑Mutation Gene Repair, Paving Way for Universal Therapies
prime_assembly_universal_gene_therapies.summary: A new Nature paper shows prime assembly can stitch long DNA fragments into precise genome sites, correcting many mutations with a single approach.
highlights: Prime assembly writes DNA flaps that capture matching gene‑sized fragments for precise insertion
The method avoids double‑strand breaks and works in non‑dividing cells, reducing toxicity
It builds on prime editing, offering a mutation‑agnostic strategy for diseases with hundreds of variants

human_organoid_mice.headline: Stanford Researchers Create Half‑Human Mice Hosting Human Brain Organoids
human_organoid_mice.summary: Scientists at Stanford University engineered mice with half a brain replaced by human cerebral organoids, revealing human pyramidal neurons and large‑scale social‑cognition cells in vivo.
highlights: Neuro‑chimeric mice contain human cerebral organoids grown inside a genetically reduced mouse brain
Human pyramidal projection neurons were detected in the chimeric brains and some migrated into spinal cords
Super‑sized neurons linked to social cognition, previously seen only in elephants, whales and primates, appeared in the mice

jwst_brown_dwarf_class.headline: JWST Uncovers Record‑Low‑Mass Brown Dwarfs in IC 348 Star Cluster
jwst_brown_dwarf_class.summary: A deeper JWST survey of the IC 348 region identified 39 candidates, confirming nine brown dwarfs as light as 2 MJup, redefining the low‑mass limit of star formation.
highlights: 39 new brown‑dwarf candidates were found in IC 348
Spectra of 15 objects revealed nine sub‑stellar members with masses down to ≈2 MJup
All 11 brown dwarfs showing a 3.4 µm aliphatic hydrocarbon feature define a new spectral class H
Two of the faintest objects exhibit circumstellar‑disk excess, hinting at planet‑forming material

baby_planet_elias2_24b.headline: New ‘Baby’ Planet Elias 2‑24 b Sets Record as Youngest Known World
baby_planet_elias2_24b.summary: Astronomers have confirmed that the Jupiter‑mass planet Elias 2‑24 b, less than a million years old, is orbiting a star 450 light‑years away, shattering previous age records.
highlights: Elias 2‑24 b is under one‑million‑year‑old, making it the youngest confirmed exoplanet
The planet was detected in archival coronagraph data from the W. M. Keck Observatory
Its discovery challenges planet‑formation models that predict Jupiter‑size planets need ~5 million years to form

tno_surface_origin.headline: Surface Colors Reveal Origins of Tiny Trans‑Neptunian Objects
tno_surface_origin.summary: New JWST and Hubble observations show that even the smallest TNOs retain surface color signatures that distinguish cold‑origin from hot‑origin bodies.
highlights: Cold TNOs display uniformly reddish surfaces while hot TNOs show a broader color range
The size distributions of hot and cold TNOs are statistically similar, implying comparable collision histories
Fewer small TNOs are observed than predicted by planetary formation models

microbes_adhesive_materials.headline: Engineered E. coli Turns Glucose into High‑Performance Hot‑Melt Adhesives
microbes_adhesive_materials.summary: Researchers at KAIST engineered Escherichia coli to produce aromatic polyhydroxyalkanoate polymers from glucose, achieving adhesive strength surpassing commercial petroleum‑based hot‑melt glues.
highlights: Poly(4HB‑co‑PhLA) reached a lap‑shear strength of 4.58 MPa, exceeding the 4.20 MPa of commercial EVA adhesive
Fed‑batch fermentation yielded up to 52.8 g L⁻¹ of poly(3HB‑co‑4HB‑co‑PhLA)
The polymers retain adhesion after repeated melting, and are enzymatically degradable

2609_18168v1.headline: Varying Higgs VEV May Resolve Primordial Element Discrepancies, Study Finds
2609_18168v1.summary: A 1.58% increase in the Higgs vacuum expectation value during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis aligns helium, deuterium and lithium abundances with observations, but implies non‑standard cosmology.
highlights: A 1.58% uplift of the Higgs VEV during BBN produces agreement with the new primordial 4He measurement by the EMPRESS group.
Deuterium abundance from Lyman‑alpha forest absorption lines and lithium on the Spite plateau are simultaneously matched.
A 0.2% Higgs VEV increase partially eases the cosmic Li problem while remaining consistent with CMB constraints.

arxiv_2609_18552v1.headline: Dark Subhaloes Impart Rotation‑Like Signals in Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxies
arxiv_2609_18552v1.summary: Controlled N‑body simulations show that encounters with dark matter subhaloes generate transient, rotation‑like kinematic features detectable in dwarf spheroidal stellar velocity fields.
highlights: Rotation‑like patterns appear in line‑of‑sight velocities despite initially non‑rotating stellar components
Plane‑of‑sky velocities exhibit alternating expansion, contraction, and opposite streaming directions
Power‑spectrum analysis quantifies spatial scales and strengthens with more massive subhaloes
Recovering the full velocity‑space signature typically requires about O(10^{4}) stellar tracers

2609_18912v1.headline: ZTF Detects First Strongly Lensed Superluminous Supernova SN 2025wny at Record Redshift
2609_18912v1.summary: Astronomers confirm SN 2025wny as the first strongly lensed SLSN‑I, finding its discovery rate aligns with simulations of ZTF’s seven‑year survey.
highlights: SN 2025wny is multiply imaged by two foreground galaxies at zₗ = 0.375
The source lies at zₛ = 2.015, making it the highest‑redshift galaxy‑scale lensed supernova
Simulated ZTF detection rate of 0.037^{+0.022}_{-0.020} yr⁻¹ matches the observed 0.14^{+0.31}_{-0.11} yr⁻¹

z7_cgm_enrichment.headline: Dense Metal‑Rich CGM Absorber Linked to Dust‑Obscured Galaxy at z≈7
z7_cgm_enrichment.summary: Astronomers discovered a dense, metal‑rich circumgalactic absorber at z = 7.03, driven by a heavily dust‑obscured starburst galaxy only visible in long‑wavelength JWST imaging.
highlights: The absorber shows the strongest equivalent widths and column densities recorded beyond redshift 5
Host galaxy ND1 lies just ~16 kpc from the quasar sightline and is detected only in JWST/NIRCam long‑wavelength bands
Outflow rate of 64 M⊙ yr⁻¹ and mass‑loading factor η≈3 indicate a powerful, metal‑laden wind
Enhanced [C/O] ratio hints at nucleosynthesis from Population III supernovae

2609_17665v1.headline: New Bayesian Study Limits Active Galactic Nucleus Contribution to LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA Binary Black Hole Mergers
2609_17665v1.summary: A unified hierarchical analysis of GWTC‑5.0 events and the Quaia AGN catalogue finds that no more than about half of observed mergers can originate from AGN discs.
highlights: Unified likelihood combines spatial correlation and population inference for the AGN fraction $f_{\rm agn}$
Using GWTC‑5.0 and Quaia, the study excludes $f_{\rm agn}\geq0.52$ for AGN with $L_{\rm bol}\ge10^{44.5}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$
Constraints tighten to $f_{\rm agn}\geq0.41$ for $L_{\rm bol}\ge10^{45.5}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and $f_{\rm agn}\geq0.61$ for

arxiv_2609_17894v1.headline: Graph Neural Networks Accelerate Disequilibrium Chemistry Modeling for Exoplanet Atmospheres
arxiv_2609_17894v1.summary: A new graph neural network surrogate reduces chemistry computation errors three‑fold, matching JWST and Ariel precision for most simulated exoplanet atmospheres.
highlights: GNN treats chemical species as nodes and temperature‑dependent reaction rates as edges
Mean abundance error drops by ~3× versus prior U‑Net model
Only ~7% of test cases exceed 20 ppm spectral error, within JWST/Ariel limits

youngest_exoplanet_elias.headline: Newborn Jupiter‑Mass Exoplanet Elias 2‑24 b Discovered at 450 Light‑Years
youngest_exoplanet_elias.summary: Astronomers identified Elias 2‑24 b, a Jupiter‑mass planet less than one million years old, orbiting a star 450 light‑years away within its natal debris disk.
highlights: Planet mass comparable to Jupiter despite its extreme youth
Age estimated at under one million years, the youngest known exoplanet
Located 450 light‑years from Earth in a gap of a protoplanetary disk
Discovery made by re‑analyzing archival coronagraph data from the W.M. Keck Observatory

pluto_liquid_nitrogen_flow_evidence.headline: New Horizons Finds Evidence of Liquid Nitrogen Flow on Pluto’s Sputnik Planitia Glacier
pluto_liquid_nitrogen_flow_evidence.summary: Scientists analyzing New Horizons images have identified dark markings that suggest liquid nitrogen may have risen through cracks and wetted Pluto’s frozen surface in recent times.
highlights: Dark features on Sputnik Planitia resemble terrestrial ice‑sheet wetting patterns
Computer models show nitrogen ice can melt at the glacier’s base and rise upward
The study appears in the peer‑reviewed Planetary Science Journal

z7_halo_masses.headline: JADES Uses Galaxy Pairs to Measure Dark Matter Halos at Cosmic Dawn
z7_halo_masses.summary: Using JWST [O III] spectroscopy of ten early‑Universe galaxy pairs, JADES estimates halo masses at z≈7, revealing a high stellar‑to‑halo mass ratio.
highlights: Dynamical mass estimators recover halo masses with ~0.2 dex scatter in the TNG100 simulation
Mean halo mass measured is log⁡(M₍₂₀₀₎/M⊙)=11.06±0.21 for galaxies with log⁡(M/M⊙)=9
